text:
maria: Heads up — linkcheck is spamming failures on CI for the Windows build only. Lots of 'fragment not found' on pages with emoji in headings.

ton y: hmm, Windows build? are these paths using backslashes anywhere in generated anchors?

maria: I inspected one example: the heading is "Deployments ⚙️ (Windows)" and the generated anchor in the HTML is `deployments-%F0%9F%9B%A7-windows` but linkcheck is looking for `deployments-windows` (no emoji).

docs-bot: linkcheck job #3421 failed: 18 broken fragments (mkdocs-windows). See: https://ci.redwood/3421

shane: I think this is due to our slugify/slugifier behaving differently on linux vs windows locale for unicode/emoji. We normalize on build but linkcheck canonicalization differs.

ev an: can we just add explicit header ids in frontmatter where these show up? e.g. `## Deployments {#deployments-windows}` — quick but manual.

maria: that would work but there are ~30 headings across docs and new ones keep appearing from examples. I'd prefer a generator fix.

shane: option A: add a mkdocs plugin config to consistently strip emoji and normalize to ascii for slugs. e.g. in `mkdocs.yml`:

```yaml
plugins:
  - slugify:
      normalize: true
      strip_emoji: true
```

(placeholder plugin name — we have to pick one or write a tiny preprocessor)

tony: we already use `mkdocs-awesome-pages-plugin` and `markdown-extensions`. Might need a tiny pre-build script that rewrites headings to add `{#explicit-id}` when emoji detected.

maria: I put together a tiny Python script that detects emoji/unicode in headings and writes explicit ids. It runs in CI pre-build. Quick diff: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4802

docs-bot: PR 4802 opened by maria — title: "ci: add heading-idizer to normalize emoji anchors"

shane: looked at the script — neat. one nit: use slug from `python-slugify` to keep consistency with other slugs. Also add a test for Windows path normalization (`\r\n` handling).

maria: added slugify + test. pushed.

tony: can we also update linkcheck to use the same slug transformation function so both sides match? maybe import the same small lib in the linkcheck runner.

ev an: yes — i'll wire linkcheck to call `slugify(slug_input)` before checking fragment existence. small change in the runner.

maria: CI run #3429 shows linkcheck now passes for mkdocs-windows matrix. :tada:

shane: nice. follow-up: create a docs style note about avoiding emoji in core headings or using explicit ids for stable links. I'll PR that.

maria: created note in CONTRIBUTING.md and referenced the PR.

tony: thumbs up. once this merges, we can add a short changelog entry about linkcheck consistency.

maria: thanks everyone — deploying patch to production docsite tomorrow morning. :rocket:
